name: veterinary_clinic_system_048_appointment_reason_triage
instruction: Triage-tag upcoming appointments and the open waitlist, then produce a triage summary, all batched under the episode batch code. The triage rules are applied to the free-text reason, case-insensitive: 'urgent' if the reason contains 'vomit', 'limping', 'lameness', or 'ear infection'; 'routine' if it contains 'wellness', 'vaccine', or 'weight management'; 'standard' for everything else. (1) For every appointment with appointment_date >= episode_date and status in ('scheduled', 'confirmed'), add triage_tier using these rules. (2) For every waitlist row with status 'waiting', set triage_tier using the same rules on its reason, and set slot_status to 'booked' if that patient has any scheduled or confirmed appointment with appointment_date >= episode_date; otherwise 'open'. (3) Create exactly one ops_reports row with report='triage_summary', batch_code, and summary = {appt_counts: {urgent: U, routine: R, standard: S}, waitlist_counts: {urgent: Wu, routine: Wr, standard: Ws}, urgent_unbooked: count of waiting waitlist rows with triage_tier='urgent' and slot_status='open'}. Past appointments and appointments with other statuses stay untouched. Existing waitlist rows are updated in place; all other collections stay untouched.
_steps_note: par_steps and max_steps must be measured against a live container in the QC session; do not set final values without a real gold run.

success_criteria.summary: Each future scheduled/confirmed appointment gets the correct triage_tier. Each waiting waitlist row gets the correct triage_tier and slot_status (booked iff the patient has a future scheduled/confirmed appointment). Exactly one triage_summary ops_reports row with correct per-tier counts and urgent_unbooked. Dual-path (raw-row Python + SQL) verification of all counts.

checks.expect: per-row triage_tier and slot_status checks; exact ops_reports summary; untouched non-target rows
appt and waitlist tier counts, and urgent_unbooked, agree between raw-row Python and SQL

hazards: The waitlist has a seeded 'priority' field that does NOT match the reason-based triage_tier. Row id 2 has priority='urgent' but reason='Anal gland expression' (standard). Row id 6 has priority='routine' but reason='Ear infection re-check' (urgent). A solution that copies the priority field will fail.

The waitlist also has slot_status hazards: row id 3 (patient 11, Dental prophylaxis consult) and row id 4 (patient 15, Dental prophylaxis consult) both have scheduled/confirmed future appointments in the snapshot (id 546 on 2026-09-30 and id 69 on 2026-09-30), so for episode 2026-09-30 their slot_status must be 'booked'. A solution using requested_date or priority instead of an actual future appointment will set them wrong.

Stale scheduled/confirmed appointments with dates before the episode date are not tagged. Row id 74 (scheduled, 2026-09-27, Ear infection re-check, provider 3) and row id 60 (scheduled, 2026-09-27, Chronic kidney disease monitoring, provider 2) are before episode 2026-09-30. Even though their reason is urgent/serious, they are in the past and must not receive triage_tier.

Keyword boundary cases: 'Annual wellness exam' is routine (wellness). 'Annual check' (id 545, scheduled, 2026-09-30) is standard because it does not contain 'wellness'. 'Vaccine boosters due' is routine, 'Vomiting since yesterday' is urgent, 'Chronic kidney disease monitoring' is standard (no keyword match), 'Skin allergy flare-up' is standard, 'Ear infection re-check' is urgent.

Status filter matters: 'checked_in' rows like id 48 (checked_in, 2026-09-04, Ear infection re-check) are on a past date and have status 'checked_in', not 'scheduled'/'confirmed', so they must not be tagged even though the reason is urgent.
Idempotency: the triage_summary row must be deleted and rewritten per batch_code so a rerun reaches the same end-state; otherwise duplicate summary rows accumulate.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses free-text keyword triage of future appointments with waitlist triage and a real booked-vs-open slot reconciliation, producing a cross-collection summary. The waitlist's existing 'priority' field is a decoy, and the summary's urgent_unbooked metric requires joining waitlist reason triage to appointment existence. No public benchmark combines these three sub-problems with reason-based triage and waitlist slot reconciliation.
